item.title: Motikiai Murray suspended for four matches following dangerous tackle
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians forward Motikiai Murray has been suspended for four matches following a dangerous tackle during the Flying Fijians’ Test match against Japan on Saturday. Murray was issued a red card for an offence under Law 9.13, which relates to dangerous tackling, after the incident was reviewed and upgraded by the Foul Play Review Officer.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians forward Motikiai Murray has been suspended for four matches following a dangerous tackle during the Flying Fijians’ Test match against Japan on Saturday.

Murray was issued a red card for an offence under Law 9.13, which relates to dangerous tackling, after the incident was reviewed and upgraded by the Foul Play Review Officer.

The team is now preparing for its upcoming Nations Championship match against France, with head coach Jake White and his coaching staff conducting an intensive three-day camp in Lyon.

White says the camp is an important opportunity for the coaching staff to assess players’ performances, combinations and overall readiness ahead of the match.

He says the final squad is yet to be confirmed, with the official team expected to be announced on Friday.

The Flying Fijians will face France next Sunday at 8.10am, before taking on Ireland on 15th November and Italy on 22nd November.

The Flying Fijians have climbed to ninth place in the latest World Rugby rankings following their 34–28 victory over Japan.

Fiji have accumulated 77.85 ranking points, moving ahead of Wales, who are in 10th place with 76.38 points.

item.title: Fiji Bati must beat New Zealand to keep semi-final hopes alive
item.description: The Fiji Bati will need to beat New Zealand this Saturday to keep their semi-final hopes alive at the Rugby League World Cup. The Bati will face New Zealand at 4.30pm at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast in a crucial Pool A match.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Bati will need to beat New Zealand this Saturday to keep their semi-final hopes alive at the Rugby League World Cup.

The Bati will face New Zealand at 4.30pm at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast in a crucial Pool A match.

Australia currently leads the men's Pool A standings with four points, followed by New Zealand in second place with two points and Fiji in third, also with two points.

The Cook Islands sit fourth after playing two matches without recording a win.

In the men's Pools B and C standings, Samoa leads with four points after winning both matches, while Tonga also has four points.

England and Papua New Guinea have two points each, while Lebanon and France are yet to record a point .

Vodafone Fiji Bati star Kurt Donoghoe believes the performance of Fiji's forwards against Australia last Sunday proves they can match New Zealand's powerful pack in Saturday's must-win Rugby League World Cup clash

In the women's competition, Australia leads Pool A with four points, followed by Samoa and England, who have two points each, while Wales is yet to register a point.

In Pool B, New Zealand is leading with 2 points, Fiji in second with two points, then Papua New Guinea with one point. France comes in at fourth who have yet to get points.

item.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Men's Ballon d'Or
item.description: Meanwhile, Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas has won the Women's Ballon d'Or after leading her club to a historic quadruple during the 2025-2026 season. Barcelona won the Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and UEFA Women's Champions League under Putellas' leadership.
item.content:encoded:
Meanwhile, Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas has won the Women's Ballon d'Or after leading her club to a historic quadruple during the 2025-2026 season.

Barcelona won the Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and UEFA Women's Champions League under Putellas' leadership.

Putellas also became Barcelona's joint-second all-time leading goalscorer after scoring twice in the Champions League semi-final in May, earning the Player of the Tournament award.

The Spanish international also played a key role in Spain's Nations League-winning campaign.

Speaking after receiving the award, Putellas thanked France Football and those who believed she deserved the honour.

She also congratulated the other nominees and winners, while acknowledging her Barcelona team-mates for their contribution to the club's success.

Putellas said it was a great honour to play alongside her team-mates, highlighting how they overcame injuries, difficulties and unexpected challenges throughout the season.

She also expressed pride in leading the team as captain.
